reason: The boot library's product duties are kept as Go package internal/boot: layered launch environment with the launch-only name rule, profile and layer composition, best-effort start with a required-entry audit, the fatal exit path and the config dump. Its Node duties (runtime module resolution, version ranges, worker bootstrap, plugin display metadata read from package.json) have no subject because components are compiled in.

The three launcher facts are kept as services provided before the tree mounts: the app's words in launch.Data, and readiness and the exit request in launch.App. The commander adapter becomes the harness-owned command-line Spec of the commander library spec, so no component sees a parsing library.

Its result (validate a candidate, write the profile layer keeping comments, reconcile, refuse an edit a higher layer shadows) is given by config.Service over the loader's one writable layer. The file is no longer parsed a second time by this package, a merge operation replaces the whole-config override, and a cross-process lock and a revision check are added.

Configuration reload is kept: the loader's layer source watches the layer files and applies changes on one serial loop, gated by this area's static check and switched on by the boot.reload component after readiness. JavaScript module replacement, module file comparison and package-cache invalidation are not built because the Go host never replaces code in process.

The management surface is kept (list, inspect, enable, disable, add, remove, one service shared by the command line, the web page and a model-facing tool, protected management entries) but over loader entries and operator-placed plugin directories. Every pnpm, registry, Git, update, build-approval and version-exemption operation is gone under DH-ADR-13.

The package reads plugin indexes so that a user can discover and install npm bundles. DH-ADR-13 decides that plugins come from local directories with no download or discovery, so there is no index to read; the reader's safety rules are recorded in DH-ADR-BOOT-11 for a later registry design.

Exists only because profile packages are resolved through Node's internal ESM and CommonJS resolvers and a native builtin-access addon. Go components are linked at build time and named through the build catalogue.
Exists only because Node caches the real path of every resolved package link, so a moved npm package cannot be remapped without a restart. The Go host maps no package directories.
Describes how linked npm package directories take part in Node's ancestor node_modules lookup. There is no node_modules lookup in a Go binary.
Exists only because a source launch uses an ESM-only Node loader hook while CommonJS requests need built files. Go has one build and no module formats.

The cause is a replay mode that swaps the config file by its basename. The Go launcher has no config-file argument and no swap: a replay run names its replay configuration as an explicit overlay layer, which takes the same path through composition as any other overlay.
The Go launch environment is also read once at launch, from the invocation directory and the home, and does not search parent directories or follow a workspace selected later.
justification: Deliberate boundary of DH-ADR-BOOT-4: a launch fact that could change after the tree exists would make config dumps and expression results differ from what runs, and would let a workspace chosen at run time change host configuration. Per-workspace variables for commands belong to the child environment that the execution area builds. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BOOT-2.

reason: The cause is that an id-targeted patch replaces the whole config. The Go layer model has a merge operation that deep-merges into config, so an override states only the fields it changes and keeps receiving the bundle's other fields.

The cause is a split at the first word the launcher does not recognise. The Go grammar splits at the profile name: launcher options come before it and every later word belongs to the app, so a launcher option written after an app option is reported as an unknown app option instead of being silently reassigned, and the launcher no longer consumes a double dash.

The cause is that a service's provider is not declared anywhere static. Each catalogue item declares the services its component may provide, so the static check reports, before anything starts and in the preview commands, an enabled entry that injects a service no entry in the composition provides.

The cause is whole-config replacement, which drops the expressions of fields the user did not mean to change. A merge operation leaves untouched fields and their expressions to the lower layer, and an edit that targets a computed field is refused unless the operation says to overwrite it.
The Go harness also writes run-time edits only to the profile layer; the home layer and command-line overlays are read for precedence and are never write targets.
justification: DH-ADR-LOADER-4 fixes exactly one writable layer so that a run-time change has one home, and DH-ADR-BOOT-2 fixes which. The cost is bounded: an edit that a higher layer shadows is refused with that layer's name and file, and the home layer and overlays are plain files whose hand edits are picked up by the same reload. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BOOT-7.

reason: The cause is that the editor stores a complete config override, which pins every field at its current raw value. config.Service writes a merge operation holding only the edited fields, so later bundle changes to the other fields still arrive.

The cause is that only rows of the root include with a unique patch id can be addressed. In Go every bundle entry must carry an explicit id (a build test checks it) and an operation addresses an entry by its path in the composed tree, so entries inside groups are editable at any depth. A preset that runs a tree of its own is edited through that tree's layers, which area A27 owns.

Module replacement through Node loader internals and the loader.exit hook for framework changes exist only because Node can swap modules in a running process. The Go host never replaces code; a new binary is a restart.
Concerns detecting changes to package.json files and the browser client's separate module graph. The Go host reads no package manifests and has no client module graph.
Describes the difference between static and dynamic JavaScript imports, Worker threads and the TSX loader during module replacement. None exists in a Go binary.
Describes how symbolic links under a profile's node_modules widen the set of JavaScript files compared for replacement. There is no node_modules tree and no file comparison.

The comparison records are the per-instance table of loaded JavaScript module files. The Go reload compares the content of layer files only, and that state belongs to the loader's layer source, which a reconfiguration of the reload component does not reset.

Describes a replaced JavaScript module that fails to import after the old one was evicted from Node's cache. No module is replaced in Go. The plugin-process analogue (a restarted plugin that fails stays failed and is reported) is owned by area A22, and a configuration edit with a static error never stops the previous instance.

The compatibility checks compare npm version ranges (engines.dsh and peer ranges) of packages changed outside the manager. First-party components carry the binary's version, and a plugin process is checked by its protocol version at every start, which area A22 owns.
Concerns the packed loader of the in-browser WebWorker preview runtime, which is JavaScript-only and dropped by DH-ADR-17.

The limit comes from comparing file modification times of loaded JavaScript modules against a marker file. The Go layer watch compares file content, so timestamp granularity and clock skew on network filesystems do not matter.
A hard link from pnpm's store keeping an older modification time defeats upstream's time-based module comparison. There is no pnpm store and no time-based comparison in Go.

The cause is that a dependency-only manifest change does not trigger recomposition, so an install made outside the manager is not seen. In Go a plugin is an entry in the profile layer: adding it by hand is a layer edit that the same reload applies, and replaced plugin files take effect when that entry is restarted.
TSX loaders and application-created Worker threads are Node runtime features outside upstream's package-cache refresh. Neither exists in Go.
Concerns CommonJS request resolution and synchronous Node resolve hooks. There is no CommonJS in a Go binary.
Future work on keeping Node's package-configuration invalidation across disposal of the hot-reload plugin. The Go host has no package-configuration cache.
Concerns assigning replaced JavaScript plugin callbacks to instances that share a runtime. No code is replaced in process in Go.

The cause is an operating-system notification stream that starts after the watcher reports readiness, so an early write is missed. Layer files are watched by a poll that compares content against the text read at boot, so a write at any moment after that read is seen at the next poll.

The pending group is pnpm's list of dependency build scripts awaiting approval. No package manager runs in Go, so there are no build scripts to approve; capability grants for a plugin are selected one by one.

The stale approval is a key in pnpm-workspace.yaml for a git-hosted npm package. That file does not exist in Go; a plugin's grants live in its own entry, are deleted with it, and are void when its manifest digest changes.
The failure is pnpm verifying lockfile tarball URLs against its default npm registry. There is no lockfile and no registry.
Concerns how an npm registry update saves version specs and where a reinstalled bundle lands in the bundle order. There are no registry updates, and a profile's bundle order is fixed in the binary.

The cause is an update made of two separate profile operations. The Go manager has no update operation; every management operation is one write of the profile layer under one lock followed by reconciliation, so no other operation can run inside it. Replacing a plugin is a restart of its entry.
Concerns reachability checks and reinstall behaviour for npm bundles fetched from Git through pnpm. Nothing is fetched in Go.
Concerns console prompts and timeouts of the Git transport probe that precedes a pnpm install. The Go manager starts no Git process.
Concerns pnpm build-script approval during an npm version update. There are no updates and no build scripts.

The cause is that the host itself loads a package's JavaScript, so a replaced package needs a new process. A plugin's code runs in its own process, so a replaced directory takes effect by restarting that one entry, in any profile, and the host is never restarted for it.

The cause is that a start-up-only profile cannot unload modules it loaded, so their package cannot be removed while it runs. In Go a management change always reconciles the running tree whether or not file watching is on, and removal unloads the entry's fiber and deletes no files, so a running plugin can be removed in every profile.
The running Go manager also refuses to disable or remove protected entries (required entries and its own components), manages only the profile it runs in, and does not edit a preset's own tree.
justification: Self-protection is kept on purpose so that the management surface cannot remove itself or a required entry. Another profile is managed from the command line, which composes that profile without a running host, and preset composition is owned by area A27. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BOOT-9.

reason: The cause is that an operation spans a package-manager run that writes many files and cannot be undone. A Go operation writes one file atomically and downloads, copies and deletes nothing, so the only split outcome is saved but not applied, which the result reports as two separate facts.
Browser synchronisation failures belong to upstream's client plugin runtime, which loads plugin code into the page. The Go UI is rendered by the host and has no client plugin runtime.
Concerns package operations owned by the Electron desktop shell. There is no desktop application.
The limit is about icon references in a Git-hosted market index. No index reader is built, so no index icon is ever resolved.
The limit is about which installed copies a market index can update. There is no market and no update operation; an operator replaces a plugin directory and restarts its entry.
Unsigned index content cannot mislead a harness that reads no index. Signed index content is recorded in DH-ADR-BOOT-11 as a requirement for a later registry design.

The lost update is in the list of index sources, which does not exist in Go. The general cause (two writers replacing a whole list) is removed for configuration by the revision check and the lock of config.Service, and is recorded for a later registry's source list.
The limit is the index reader's refusal of HTTP redirects. No index is fetched; the refusal is recorded as a rule a later registry keeps.

The memory and event-loop cost comes from downloading and indexing a whole market document in the host. No document is downloaded; server-side queries are recorded as a requirement for a later registry.
The limit is about which branch a market entry's README is read from. No market entry pages exist; a local plugin's description comes from its own directory.
The limit is that public npm file hosts do not serve packages of private registries. Nothing is read from npm file hosts or registries.
The limit is a Git server setting needed to fetch a pinned commit for a market entry. The harness fetches nothing from Git.
The limit is the fixed list of README file names asked of GitHub and GitLab file APIs. The harness calls neither API for plugins.
The limit is anonymous access to GitHub and GitLab APIs with a clone fallback for private repositories. No repository is read for plugin listings.
The limit is that pages of a cached index document can change between reads. There is no index document and nothing to page.

title: Discovered .env layers are written into the process environment, so ordinary project variables reach every child process; the decision note records this as not solved

reason: The Go launch environment is an immutable snapshot with a recorded source per name and is never written into the process environment. Each child environment is built explicitly by the execution area, so a discovered file's values reach a child only if they are passed by name.

title: The plugin_manager tool body requests its own sandbox escalation and approval instead of declaring its effect to the tool pipeline, so the gate exists only as long as that body calls it

reason: The Go tool declares a per-action effect (read, or profile-wide change) and the guarded pipeline asks; the tool body contains no approval call, so a new action cannot forget the gate and denial is tested through the pipeline.

The Go harness exposes a changed tool of the same name with four actions: list and inspect read, attach and detach call area A22's session-scoped plugin attachment for the calling agent's own session. The install, bundle-selection and version-exemption actions are gone with pnpm and registries, and the tool has no action that changes the profile, because A22's rule (DH-ADR-EXT-8) and DH-ADR-16 forbid a consent given at a prompt from outliving the session. The tool body asks nothing; the one consent an attachment needs is an interaction asked by A22.
The tool lists the plugins of configured market indexes. With no market and no download there is nothing for it to read, so the Go harness exposes no such tool.

Replaced by the typed notify event loader.Reloaded, raised after every settled reconciliation whatever caused it. Unlike upstream's event it carries the ids created, updated, restarted and removed and the issues found, so listeners need not re-read the tree to learn what changed.

The event reports a watched file that is neither a module nor a configuration file. The Go host watches layer files only and reloads no code, so no general file-change event exists; template and asset edits during UI development are a build concern.
The event announces finished module replacements. No module is replaced in Go; the one notification after a reload settles is loader.Reloaded, which also covers an entry restarted on request.

Kept as the typed notify event plugins.Changed with the entry ids whose listing changed. It is derived from loader.Reloaded, so a change made by a hand edit of a layer file is announced too, which upstream's event does not do.
The event streams the output of a pnpm run. No package manager or other child process runs during a management operation; an operation's diagnostic is in its result.

The event reports the phases of an installation across registries (installing, cancelling, applying). Adding a plugin is one validated write followed by reconciliation, with no phases and nothing to cancel.

Kept as the typed notify event plugins.Operation with an operation id, action, target id, phase and outcome, raised on the manager's own goroutine after the caller has its result so that a listener never delays an operation. It carries no directory path, grant list or error text.
The event reports the steps of a bundle update (checking, removing, installing, restoring). DH-ADR-13 excludes updates: an operator replaces the directory.
The event announces a change to the configured market index sources. There are no index sources.

Replaced by the Go struct reload.Config with one field, Debounce (100 ms). The module watch fields base, root and ignored and the watcher options are gone with module replacement, and disabling the boot.reload entry is the switch for applying changes at the next start.

Replaced by the Go struct plugins.Config with LockWait (10 s) and InspectMaxBytes (1 MiB). The fourteen other upstream fields configure pnpm, npm registries, Git probes, version listings and npm file hosts, none of which exists.
Every field configures the index reader (sources, fetch limits, caches, Git timeouts, file hosts). The reader is not built.

Replaced by service key config.Key with interface config.Service: Tree, Preview, Apply and Status. It keeps validate-then-write-then-reconcile and the refusal of a shadowed edit, and adds a preview that starts nothing, a revision check, merge operations and a cross-process lock.

No Go service takes its place. Its exclusive queue is the layer source's serial loop reached through config.Service.Apply, its configuration watch is the loader's layer watch switched on by the boot.reload component, a restart of one entry is the loader's Restart, and its module methods have no subject.

Replaced by service key plugins.Key with interface plugins.Manager: List, Inspect, Add, SetEnabled, Restart and Remove. The package, registry, version, exemption and detail-document methods are gone under DH-ADR-13.
The service reads and searches market indexes. No index reader is built.

Replaced by service key launch.Key holding the immutable launch.Data (profile, home, working directory, version, terminal flag, overlay paths, app words), with launch.EnvKey and launch.AppKey beside it. The package-manager invocation and the installation anchor are gone, and the telemetry opt-out value moves to the launcher layer.

Kept: one precedence order (launcher layer, overlays, home layer, profile layer, bundles, then the environment a value's expression reads, then the Go default) and the rule that a discovered .env may not set launch-only names, with proxy and endpoint names accepted from the home file only. Changed: the snapshot is never written into the process environment, which the note itself lists as not solved. The note's settings.yaml tier is already superseded upstream; credential ordering belongs to area A17.

Kept with one tightening: the application, not the framework, owns the required entry ids (a Required list on each built-in profile definition, built from one shared spine list plus the profile's carrier set), a failing disabled expression is a failure and not a skip, and the audit runs only at boot. Changed so that it fails closed: a required id must also be present and enabled, and a layer that removes or disables one is a static issue, where upstream ignores an absent id and so lets a profile lose its carrier. A settle deadline is added because a Go component can block forever while loading.

The note computes one immutable table from package names to npm package directories and installs it into Node's resolvers. Node resolution does not exist in Go. Its goal, one immutable and inspectable answer to what code each configured name means, is met by the build catalogue that the loader uses as its resolver.

Kept: the command line, the web page and the tool call the same operations under one profile lock; profile files remain the persisted state; a toggle edits only the disabled field; saved state and activation are reported separately. Replaced: pnpm operations and build-script approvals are gone, and the queue shared with module replacement is the layer source's serial loop.

Kept: the host inspects before anything is added and reports a specific problem, and a failed operation leaves no half-installed state. The mechanism differs: inspection reads a local directory through area A22's inspector, A22 makes the approved copy before the entry is written, and because the management operation itself is one write of one file there are no profile files to snapshot and restore and no run to cancel; a copy whose entry was never written is unreferenced and is removed by retention.

The goal is kept for one session and no longer for the profile: an agent adds a capability mid-conversation by attaching a local plugin directory it authored to its own session through plugin_manager, after one consent from an owner, and the plugin runs as a confined process, not host code. The persistence is dropped on purpose: area A22 (DH-ADR-EXT-8) rules that no tool call can make a plugin durable or host-wide, which applies DH-ADR-16; a durable installation is an owner's action in the command line or the plugins page. The cordis_inspect tool the note mentions belongs to area A22.

The note plans npm registries and mirrors for pnpm installs. DH-ADR-13 excludes download, so there is no registry to plan. The first verdict expected its goals to carry to a Go download source; none exists, and the rule that a private source never falls back to a public one is recorded in DH-ADR-BOOT-11 for a later registry.

Exists only because of Node module resolution and the npm package layout: it defines the ancestor node_modules search inside a profile. Go components are linked at build time and plugin processes share no modules with the host.

Kept: an uncaught failure is fatal, reported once and never resumed, with a release hook under a fixed bound; boot owns that one exit path and area A18 owns the diagnostic's content and file. The best-effort spill rule is area A07's. The desktop crash-report dialog has no subject under DH-ADR-18 and becomes the diagnostic file; the client batch retry has no subject under DH-ADR-3.

The goal stands: a running host follows plugin adds, switches and removals without a restart. The mechanism (publishing a module-resolution generation and expiring Node's package caches) has no Go counterpart; a plugin is an entry, so reconciliation starts or stops the fiber that owns its process.

Kept: all recomposition goes through one exclusive path, and replacing a plugin is a stop followed by a start. Replaced: Node module eviction is gone; a replaced plugin directory takes effect when its entry is restarted, and an entry whose manifest changed refuses to start until it is inspected and granted again.

The note adds host-owned updates from npm registries and Git. DH-ADR-13 excludes updates: the operator replaces a directory by hand. The first verdict expected a Go version source and rollback; none is designed until a registry is.

The rule is kept: a failed management operation always shows its diagnostic, and what the caller sees agrees with the log. It is met differently: there is no output stream that a diagnostic could be missing from, because every operation returns its problems and issues in its result.

The note adds a market index reader, a Discover page and a read-only tool. DH-ADR-13 excludes discovery, so none is built. The first verdict kept the reader's rules for a redesigned install path; they are recorded in DH-ADR-BOOT-11 (only configured sources, no redirects, bounded size) for a later registry.

A repair of two test cases in upstream's own suite, which exists only as part of the upstream build and test process. Its lesson, that a test waits on the state it asserts and not on the clock, is the virtual-time rule of the Go toolchain decisions.

A repair of two upstream test files after a CI host leaked Git command-line configuration into Git child processes, part of the upstream test process. The Go plugin manager starts no Git process at all.

Adopted. The proposal keeps serialized live configuration refresh, readiness coordination and disposal drainage and removes module replacement with its Node-loader coupling. That is the Go design: the layer source reloads configuration, and a code change is a new binary or a restart of one plugin entry.

Adopted by construction. The Go boot package has one way to locate configuration (the home and the profile name) and one environment loader (the layered launch environment); the older path resolver with its basename swap and the single-file loader are not built.

title: A profile is a compiled-in definition plus one layer file; bundles are embedded layers
The layer order is fixed, and the profile layer is the one writable layer
Components are declared in an explicit build catalogue
Launch facts are frozen before the tree, and a discovered file cannot change how the harness starts
Expressions read only frozen, declared, secret-free data
Start-up is best effort with one required list, one readiness signal, one fatal path and a bounded shutdown
A change is checked as a whole before anything is applied
Hosts that share a profile coordinate through the file and a lock, not through each other
A cleanup that does not return is named, never force-released
The plugin manager manages entries and local directories for an owner; the model's tool can only attach to its own session
Safe mode switches off plugin processes and optional bundles through the launcher layer, and nothing else
One naming rule for components, entries and groups, enforced by the catalogue
config.Service.Apply is the only run-time writer of configuration
Safe mode disables the plugins group and every optional bundle group through the launcher layer and changes nothing else
The plugin market, registries, updates and version exemptions are not built
A build knows its components by name, and says so
Launch facts, the launch environment and the expression scope
Profiles, embedded bundles and the layer stack
yamlx: one YAML dialect, with edits that keep comments
The boot sequence, the audit, readiness, the fatal path and shutdown
The composed tree can be previewed, explained and checked without starting anything
Validated reload and one edit path, safe across processes
A watchdog names a cleanup that does not return
Plugins are listed, inspected, added, switched, restarted and removed from one service
An agent attaches a plugin to its own session, and to nothing else
The catalogue rejects duplicate, nil and malformed items, and its resolver tells an unknown name from one unavailable on this platform
Every built-in profile composes through the real codec and loader: explicit ids, resolvable components, strict config, valid expressions, declared providers, a golden tree
The generated component catalogue equals a fresh render
Launch environment precedence and sources; a launch-only name in a file aborts and applies nothing; the process environment is unchanged
Home precedence, immutable launch data, readiness only after the audit, an idempotent exit request
The expression scope holds only declared, secret-free data and a wrong name fails at check time with a position
The layer stack has the stated order and exactly one writable layer; empty files, custom profiles and nested path ids behave as specified
Profile reset moves only the profile layer aside under a unique name
yamlx edits at a nested path keep every comment and expression, and a write whose re-parse differs is refused
Start-up matrix: each failure kind is a warning for an optional entry and stops start-up with a full unload for a required one
The start-up report is one golden text on standard error with positions, and standard output stays empty
Shutdown unloads leaves first, honours the status of the first stop request, ends at once on an interrupt and exits 124 at the bound
A panic on a harness goroutine takes the one fatal path with a bounded release
The dump is golden, loadable and annotated with supplying layers; check exits non-zero on a static issue; nothing is constructed
A layer edit with any static issue is rejected whole with an exact position; the corrected edit restarts only changed entries
Apply refuses stale, shadowed and computed-field edits, writes only edited fields, and reports an unsaved edit until it is written
Two layer sources on one real file and lock lose no edit, bound the lock wait and take over a dead holder's lock
With reload disabled a file edit waits for restart while Apply still reconciles; a change saved before readiness applies after it
A blocked cleanup is reported with entry, component and effect label, and later cleanups of that fiber do not run meanwhile
Plugin manager operations against a fake inspector: refusals write nothing, add writes one insert, remove leaves the directory untouched
The plugin_manager tool has list and inspect, asks nothing, never writes the profile layer, and no plugin_market tool exists
The tool's attach and detach reach the plugin service for the calling session and never write the profile layer
No init-time registration, one place that ends the process and unloads the root, one package that writes configuration, and every required id exists in its profile
A launch that cannot serve fails loudly, and one that can serve does
Two processes on one home and one profile do not lose or half-apply an edit
A local plugin directory is inspected, granted, run, replaced, removed and left off in safe mode
An agent attaches a plugin to its own session, and the profile does not change
A cleanup that never returns is named, and the process still ends
